caption:
बॉलीवुत की बेबाक राइटर Twinkle Khanna अपने नए कॉलम को लेकर ज़बरदस्त सुर्खियों में हैं! 🎭

The Times of India के अपने कॉलम में Twinkle ने रावण की तुलना दुनिया के बड़े टेक बिलियनेयर्स से की है। उन्होंने रावण को 'original tech bro' कहते हुए Jensen Huang, Elon Musk और Bill Gates जैसे दिग्गजों से उनके कनेक्शन जोड़े। 💥

Twinkle ने फिल्म Ramayana के एक्टर Ranbir Kapoor के उस पुराने बयान को याद किया, जिसमें Ranbir ने Elon Musk की Tesla Roadster और रावण के पुष्पक विमान की बात कही थी।

लेख में Twinkle ने लिखा कि रावण के पास बेहिसाब ज्ञान, ताकत, संपत्ति और तकनीक थी, लेकिन वे अपने मन पर काबू नहीं पा सके। उनके मुताबिक रावण को बस एक लेदर जैकेट, Silicon Valley HQ और 10 सिर पर डिवाइस के साथ खुद का podcast चाहिए, फिर वे आज के दौर में बिल्कुल फिट बैठेंगे। 🤯

बता दें कि Nitesh Tiwari के निर्देशन और Namit Malhotra के प्रोडक्शन में बन रही फिल्म Ramayana में Ranbir Kapoor और Yash मुख्य भूमिका में हैं।

क्या आपको भी लगता है कि Twinkle Khanna की यह तुलना सही है? कमेंट्स में अपनी राय ज़रूर बताएं! 👇

ctx.title: Twinkle Khanna calls Ravana the 'original tech bro', compares him to tech billionaires Jensen Huang, Bill Gates
ctx.summary: Twinkle Khanna draws parallels between Ravana and prominent tech billionaires, describing Ravana as a blueprint for the original tech bro.
ctx.text:
You can always trust Twinkle Khanna to have an unfiltered take on everything making news. Recently, the actor-turned-writer shared her thoughts on Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's film Ramayana . In her latest column, Twinkle compared Ravana to a few tech billionaires, including Jensen Huang, Elon Musk and Bill Gates, calling him the 'original tech bro'.
In her column for The Times of India, Twinkle recalled Ranbir Kapoor's past remark about Elon Musk's Tesla Roadster and Ravana's Pushpak Viman. Ranbir, who plays Lord Ram in Ramayana, had said, “India invented a flying car 5,000 years ago.”
Taking a cue from Ranbir's observation, Twinkle described Ravana as 'the blueprint for the original tech bro'. She drew parallels between the mythological king and some of the world's most powerful businessmen, referring to the controversies surrounding their personal lives and alleged affairs.
She mentioned Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his alleged affair with Alice Huang, how he had to step down from the company he had built for over three decades after the affair came to light. She also mentioned Bill Gates and the scrutiny he faced following revelations about his alleged affairs. Twinkle noted that Ravana had the intelligence and ability to conquer the world but failed to master his own mind, much like some powerful men today.
Drawing comparisons between Ravana and the billionaires, she wrote, "Ravana was exceptionally learned, wealthy, powerful and had access to remarkable tech. He also believed that he was above the rules that governed others. Add the obsession with immortality, and the similarities between him and today's tech billionaires are hard to ignore."
She further added, “All Ravana needs is a leather jacket, a device on each of his ten heads, a Silicon Valley HQ with his own podcast, and he would blend right in. Ravana had the intelligence and ability to master the world, but like so many powerful men, failed to master his own mind.”
Ramayana is a two-part cinematic adaptation of the Hindu epic, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra. The film features music by Oscar-winning composer Hans Zimmer and AR Rahman.
The first part was released on November 5, with the second part expected to follow in 2028.
Vibha Maru is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times Entertainment, based in Delhi. With a decade of experience across digital and print media, she covers Bollywood, Hollywood and web shows.

A self-confessed cinephile who breathes Hindi cinema, Vibha can often be found sacrificing sleep after binge-watching films and web series. Though she holds a Commerce degree, she discovered her true calling in journalism after enrolling at the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC). She began her career covering Delhi's cultural scene, food, nightlife, concerts, and city life at The Times of India, before moving into full-time entertainment journalism with India Today.

At India Today, Vibha interviewed some of the biggest names in Bollywood and television while carving a niche for herself through film reviews, opinion pieces, nostalgic features, celebrity interviews, and trend-driven stories. She later brought her storytelling and editorial expertise to The Indian Express, where she continued to deepen her understanding of cinema through long-form entertainment explainers, retrospectives and feature writing.
